keywords: atlas mountains day hike from marrakech
overview: Imlil is a mountain village at about 1,740 meters, 65 km south of Marrakech, where the paved road ends and the trails into Toubkal National Park begin. Mount Toubkal, at 4,167 meters the highest peak in North Africa, rises at the head of the valley. Climbing it takes two days, so this trip is a day of walking in the valley below it.

The drive takes about 1.5 hours through the Moulay Brahim gorge and the market town of Asni, which holds its weekly souk on Saturdays. In Imlil you meet a local mountain guide and walk up through walnut and apple orchards to Aroumd, a stone village on a ridge at the top of the valley with a clear view toward the high peaks.

Lunch is a home-cooked tagine with a Berber family or on a guesthouse terrace in the valley. The walk is about 3 hours in total at an easy pace, and a mule can carry you on the steeper parts if you prefer. You are back in Marrakech by early evening.

program.title: Pickup in Marrakech
program.description: Your driver collects you at your hotel, or at the nearest gate a vehicle can reach if you are staying inside the medina. You leave Marrakech heading south toward the High Atlas.

program.title: Moulay Brahim gorge and Asni
program.description: The road climbs through the red cliffs of the Moulay Brahim gorge, with photo stops at viewpoints, then passes through Asni. On Saturdays you can stop briefly at the weekly market.

program.title: Arrive in Imlil and meet your guide
program.description: Mint tea on a terrace in Imlil while you meet your local mountain guide, who will walk with you for the rest of the day.

program.title: Walk up to Aroumd
program.description: Follow mule paths through walnut and apple orchards and along irrigation channels up to Aroumd. From the village there are views up the valley toward the Toubkal massif. A mule can be arranged for the uphill part.

program.title: Lunch in the valley
program.description: A home-cooked lunch of salad, tagine and fruit with mint tea, either in a family home or on a terrace facing the mountains.

program.title: Walk back down to Imlil
program.description: Return to Imlil by a different path through the lower hamlets and orchards, with time to visit the small craft shops in the village.

program.title: Return drive to Marrakech
program.description: Drive back down the valley. You are dropped at your accommodation in Marrakech around 17:00.

includes: Pickup and drop-off at your Marrakech hotel or riad
Round-trip transport in an air-conditioned vehicle
Driver who speaks English, French, Spanish or German
excludes: Drinks other than water and mint tea
Tips for your guide and driver
goodToKnow: Wear walking shoes or trail shoes with good grip. The paths are rocky and can be loose.
Imlil is about 1,300 meters higher than Marrakech and noticeably cooler. Bring a fleece or light jacket in every season, and warm layers from November to March, when snow is common on the peaks.
The walk is about 3 hours in total at an easy pace with breaks. No hiking experience is needed.
Bring cash in dirhams for the optional mule, tips and small purchases.
This day trip does not reach the Toubkal summit. If you want to climb it, ask us about the 2-day Toubkal trek.

faqs.question: How far is Imlil from Marrakech?
faqs.answer: Imlil is about 65 km south of Marrakech, a drive of around 1.5 hours each way. The full day lasts about 9 hours.

faqs.question: Can I climb Mount Toubkal in one day from Marrakech?
faqs.answer: No. The summit is at 4,167 meters and the climb normally takes two days with a night at the refuge. This day trip walks in the valley below the mountain, up to Aroumd at about 1,900 meters.

faqs.question: How fit do I need to be for the Imlil hike?
faqs.answer: The walk suits anyone who can walk for 3 hours with breaks on uneven paths. It goes uphill for about 2 hours and down for about 1.5 hours. A mule can carry you on the uphill part if needed.

faqs.question: What is the weather like in Imlil?
faqs.answer: Imlil is much cooler than Marrakech. Summer days are pleasant, and from November to March it can be cold, with snow on the peaks and sometimes in the village. Bring warm layers in winter.

faqs.question: Is lunch included on the Imlil day trip?
faqs.answer: Yes. A home-cooked lunch of salad, tagine, fruit and mint tea is included. Tell us about vegetarian or other dietary needs when booking.
